title: Personal OKRs draft + weekly check-in
content:
Context / purpose:
- Scratchpad for my Q2 personal OKRs and weekly check-in notes.
- Will iterate this into the team OKR doc and share with manager for feedback.

Draft Objectives (top-level):
O1: Reduce serving latency tail for common gen models to improve p95 SLA
  KR1: Decrease p95 latency for text-gen-compat models from 380ms -> 300ms for 512 tokens (measured on Dedicated staging).
  KR2: Ship kernel-selection heuristics that reduce worst-case NV memory stalls by 30%.
  KR3: Run 3 production A/B rollouts of optimized kernels with no >2% regression in quality.

O2: Improve model onboarding throughput across the org
  KR1: Cut average onboarding time from 5d -> 2d (includes perf profiling + verification).
  KR2: Add 4 new automated checks to the onboarding pipeline (memory, quantization compatibility, perf regression, model card completeness).
  KR3: Create and publish 2 onboarding templates for T4 vs A100 profiles.

O3: Mentor and grow infra craftsmanship in the Platform team
  KR1: Lead 6 knowledge-share sessions (60m) on runtime internals and perf debugging.
  KR2: Pair-review 8 onboarding/infra PRs with clear feedback and follow-up tasks.
  KR3: Run a postmortem playbook trial with one on-call rotation and capture process improvements.

Notes / reasoning (rough):
- O1 is highest impact for customers (latency directly correlates w/ UX + costs). Focus on p95 rather than mean because tail impacts experienced latency.
- O2 helps us scale model catalog and reduces friction for Solutions + Research teams.
- O3 keeps team healthy and spreads knowledge so we avoid single-person bottlenecks.

Weekly check-in (2026-03-19):
- Wins:
  - Prototype kernel-selection heuristics merged to staging branch (PR linked). Initial microbench shows ~12% reduction in worst-case memory stall.
  - Finished onboarding checklist draft; Samira + Riley gave quick thumbs.
- Metrics update:
  - Staging p95 for text-gen-compat (512 tokens): 365ms (baseline 380ms) — progress but not yet at 300ms target.
  - Onboarding avg time (measured last 30d): 4.6d -> trending down after checklist.
- Blockers / risks:
  - One perf regression flagged during kernel rollout on older T4 nodes (ENG-842). Need to detect fallback scenarios earlier in the stack.
  - Need more realistic workload traces from Solutions team — current traces are too synthetic.
- Questions for manager / next steps:
  - Priority trade-off: should I continue with kernel heuristics work (medium-term payoff) or spend more time on automation that yields immediate onboarding wins?
  - Can we ask Solutions PM to share production traces this week?

Action items (this week):
- Investigate T4 regression: add guardrails to fallback policy and create a small repro (owner: me). Target: 2d spike fix. Linked Jira ENG-842.
- Ship onboarding automation: implement first two automated checks (memory, quant-compat) and enable for new model PRs (owner: Samira + me).
- Schedule knowledge-share #1: runtime internals, tentatively 2026-03-25 (owner: me).
- Add more realistic traces: reach out to Solutions team + draft email (owner: Riley).

Retro / self-reflection (last sprint):
- What went well: quick prototype iteration helped us get measurable perf wins early. Team collaboration improved velocity on onboarding checklist.
- What could be better: I spent too much time optimizing heuristics without clear acceptance criteria. Need to lock success metrics earlier.
- Improvement plan: define stop criteria for prototype phase (e.g., measurable 10% perf improvement on staging + no regressions on T4). If not met after 2 weeks, pivot to automation.

Open thoughts / brainstorm (low fidelity):
- Could we add an onboarding "canary" model that exercises edge-case kernels nightly and surface regressions to a Slack channel? Might catch T4 regressions earlier.
- Explore a lightweight model card linter as a pre-submit hook.

References / links:
- Kernel heuristics PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/987
- Jira: ENG-842 (T4 perf regression)
- Onboarding checklist: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/123456789
- Slack thread re: traces: https://slack.com/archives/C01ABCDEF/p1679182736453

- Convert this doc into a short slide for weekly 1:1.
